column1: # REQUEST-DOOR-SITES - generated by scripts/generate-request-door-sites.ps1 from bt-source's
# request_doors test (T-REQUEST-DOOR-GUARD): every failure the C1 guard meets walking each
# request door of crates/bt-app/src/window_waits.tsv's `# request-doors` to its boundary, and
# the program's implicit impls once, by site (file, item, kind, name; never a line) with the
# number of sites behind it. Verdicts: std / follows <key>; ... (read: nothing behind it),
# unreviewed (not read yet), violation (a C1 breach; the reason names its finding). Held equal to
# the tree by the test; shrink-only against the merge base by
# scripts/ci/check-request-door-sites.ps1 - a key added or grown, a verdict moved to unreviewed
# or violation or away from violation, or a follows row re-pointed, carries a new reason
# 'YYYY-MM-DD: <why>'. An unread row's reason is the one Q8 (B) gives the seed.
# 2026-11-02 (plan row 52): a door of `# request-door-cuts` is walked to its boundary from its
# enqueue; its `beside` side keeps a breach and a read row here, and 6963 unread keys met only
# beside a cut are not listed (target/request-door-sites/beside.tsv names them).
